summary:
Mission Mars: Junior Astronaut Base Trainer is an interactive space survival game developed using PictoBlox for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. The game allows young students to experience the challenges of managing a Mars base for 10 days. Players must maintain four essential systems: Oxygen, Power, Food, and Shield. Each system decreases daily, and unexpected events such as dust storms, solar flares, and machine failures create additional challenges. Players receive only three actions per day to increase their selected resources by 20%. They must make smart decisions and manage resources carefully to survive all 10 days.

Our project addresses the challenge of making space education more engaging and understandable for young learners through interactive gameplay. It introduces real-life space survival concepts while developing critical thinking, resource management, planning, and decision-making skills. We aim to inspire students to explore space science through creativity, technology, and learning by playing.
details:
Mission Mars: Junior Astronaut Base Trainer - NASA SPACE eX

Mission Mars: Junior Astronaut Base Trainer is an interactive space survival game developed using PictoBlox. It allows students to experience the challenges of managing a Mars base for 10 days.

How it works: Players control a Mars base and monitor four essential systems: Oxygen, Power, Food, and Shield. All systems start at 100% and decrease daily. Players receive three actions per day, with each action increasing one selected resource by 20%. Random events such as Dust Storms, Solar Flares, and Machine Breakdowns create unexpected challenges. Players must manage their resources carefully to survive all 10 days. If any system reaches zero or below, the mission fails.

Benefits and Impact: The game makes space science more interesting and accessible to young learners. It encourages critical thinking, problem-solving, resource management, planning, and decision-making while introducing the challenges of astronaut survival on Mars.

Tools and Technologies: We used PictoBlox and its block-based programming environment, including variables, loops, conditional statements, random number generation, broadcasts, and interactive sprites and buttons. No external hardware was required.

Creativity: Our project transforms Mars survival challenges into an interactive game with cartoon astronauts, a space-themed interface, resource indicators, and unpredictable events.

Factors Considered: We considered age-appropriate learning, simple game controls, limited resources, unexpected situations, balanced gameplay, and an engaging experience for young students.
